To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the distinction between implicit and explicit learning, and the notion of implicit knowledge, can be maintained.
implicit and explicit knowledge are not two different systems but rather two ends of a continuum of cognitive operations that can be applied in language acquisition and language processing.

the implicit and explicit learning distinction can be upheld, that it has to be conceived of as an interactional, dynamic, and probabilistic continuum rather than as a static dichotomy, and that implicit and explicit learning can be conceived of as two different types of knowledge, which are acquired through different types of learning and which have different functions in language acquisition and use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) Is the distinction between implicit and explicit learning valid?
the nature of the relationship between implicit and explicit language learning and with the nature of implicit and explicit knowledge in language acquisition.
the question of how the human brain acquires and stores language knowledge, and how this knowledge is used for the purpose of communication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
implicit and explicit knowledge are both acquired and learned and that they are both implicit and explicit.
, in general, first and second language learners are capable of implicit and explicit language learning.
implicit and explicit language learning are not two separate processes, but rather that they are two ends of a continuum, and that both are involved in language learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
implicit and explicit knowledge are not dichotomous, but rather represent two extremes of a continuum.

implicit learning is not a single phenomenon but rather a complex phenomenon with a number of different types of implicit learning, each of which may involve different brain mechanisms and may be subject to different types of learning.

, in general, two system theories appear to account for both first and second language development, and that, in general and for most learners, implicit and explicit knowledge develop simultaneously and are not mutually exclusive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in our view, Krashen's distinction between acquired and learned is still valid.
the implicit/explicit dichotomy is a useful heuristic for understanding the nature of the language faculty and language acquisition.

, although we do not have an explicit theory of the relationship between implicit and explicit learning, we can make some progress by looking at the relationship between implicit/explicit learning and implicit/explicit knowledge, which is a relationship that we do have some knowledge about.
